name: EZ Coming Soon
author: watchthedot

sections.description:
Display a fully customisable coming soon and maintenance page to your WordPress site. Use the basic pages provided by the plugin or add your own template to your child theme.

No complicated settings, and no visual builders. Just a straightforward one-button setup so you can focus on building your website.

The plugin also blocks access via the REST API and via XML-RPC so users can’t jump to see what you are building.

Full Options

  • None – Doesn’t block access to the site
  • Blank Screen – Only displays a white screen
  • Maintenance Mode – Displays maintenance mode text (Editable via the “Maintenance Mode Options” page in settings)
  • Basic Message – Displays a basic message (Editable via the “Basic Message Options” page in settings)
  • Use Template – Displays your theme’s own coming soon page: a coming_soon.php file in a classic theme, or the “Coming Soon” template in a block theme (edit it in Appearance > Editor > Templates, or add templates/coming-soon.html to your theme)
  • Login Screen – Redirects all requests to the login screen

Maintenance Mode answers with a 503 status and a Retry-After header, so search engines know the outage is temporary. The login screen, wp-admin, WP-Cron and admin-ajax keep working, and anybody with the bypass capability sees the site as normal.
sections.installation: The only place to download this plugin is from the WordPress Repo! Once downloaded, activate from the Plugins admin screen.
sections.faq:
The IP allowlist does not work behind my proxy or CDN

Turn on “My site is behind a proxy or CDN (e.g. Cloudflare)” in the settings. The allowlist then uses the visitor address the proxy passes on: CF-Connecting-IP, then the first public address in X-Forwarded-For, then X-Real-IP. Leave it off if your site is not behind a proxy, because anybody can send those headers. Developers can also return the address from the ez-coming-soon/client_ip filter.
sections.changelog:
We use the Semantic Versioning system of defining versions (https://semver.org/).
This means that version 1.10 is a minor update for the version 1.x branch and version 2.0 is a MAJOR update.
We will not wrap version numbers of double digits.

1.1.0

  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1; requires WordPress 6.5 or later
  • security: the bypass cookie is now signed and only honoured when Cookie Bypass is on. Cookies set by earlier versions no longer work; set a new one from the admin notice
  • security: the IP allowlist no longer trusts X-Real-IP or X-Forwarded-For unless you turn on the new “My site is behind a proxy or CDN (e.g. Cloudflare)” setting. If your site is behind Cloudflare or another proxy and you use the allowlist, turn that setting on after updating
  • fix: Maintenance Mode sends a 503 status with a Retry-After header
  • fix: feeds and sitemaps no longer show the site’s content while it is blocked
  • fix: Redirect to Homepage no longer loops on sites with a static front page
  • fix: Use Template works with block themes, and adds a Coming Soon template to the Site Editor (WordPress 6.7+)
  • fix: translations are no longer loaded too early, and all settings and notices can be translated
  • fix: the plugin no longer answers for classes that are not its own, which could break other plugins
  • fix: PHP 8.4 deprecation in the settings library
  • feat: settings and the bypass capability are removed when the plugin is deleted

1.0.4

  • feat: add documentation link to plugin meta

1.0.3

  • fix: issue where users couldn’t login when they had the capability check
  • fix: make the cannot login message translatable
  • feat: publish language files

1.0.2

  • fix: WP_Error and WP_User weren’t included correctly

1.0.1

  • Fix issue with vendor not being included in the build output

1.0.0

  • Initial Version

For more information, see the plugin page
